div.p: Landmark 1 / Challenge 2 / Trivia Structure
10 travel questions. Each correct answer earns 1 token. Total possible trivia reward: 10 tokens.
Keeper Opening
Since you're on your way, learn a bit about where you're going. These questions will help you later. Don't rush them. Answer each one carefully. Each correct answer earns you one token.
What year did Grand Central Terminal officially open?
Answer: 1913
Keeper hint: Michelin NYC Guide - page 180. It was opened 10 years after it was designed
Correct: Right. That's one token.
Incorrect: Not quite. Try again.
What material is the main concourse floor made from?
Answer: Marble
Acceptable: Marble; Tennessee marble; marble
Keeper hint: NYC Landmarks - page 103.
Correct: Exactly. Another token.
The main ceiling shows zodiac constellations. Why do you think the designers chose to include stars instead of a regular painted ceiling?

div.div: Because the original architect had a degree in astronomy
To create a sense of wonder and inspire travelers
To follow a city law requiring art in public buildings
To make the ceiling look higher than it actually is

div.p: Answer: To create a sense of wonder
Acceptable: To create a sense of wonder; to make people look up; to connect the station to the sky; to inspire travelers
Keeper hint: There's no single right answer here. Think about what the stars might represent. What feeling were they trying to create?
Correct: Good thinking. That's a token.
What is the name of the famous spot where people can hear each other whisper from across the room?
Answer: The Whispering Gallery
Acceptable: The Whispering Gallery; Whispering Arch; whispering gallery
Keeper hint: Lonely Planet NYC Guide - Page 185.
Correct: Correct. One more token.
The constellations on the ceiling are reversed. What is the most common explanation people give for why they're backwards?

div.div: The paint dried before it could be corrected
A perspective from God's view, looking down
The original blueprint was printed in reverse
The artist copied a medieval star map by accident

div.p: Answer: God's view
Acceptable: God's view; viewed from above; it was painted incorrectly; mistake
Keeper hint: Lonely Planet NYC Guide - Page 185.
Correct: Right. That's another token.
Why do you think the designers placed the famous brass clock at the exact center of the main concourse?

div.div: To serve as a meeting point that every traveler could spot
Because that was the only spot with enough floor space
To mark the center for the building's structural balance
To honor the Vanderbilt family tradition of clockmaking

div.p: Answer: To serve as a meeting point that every traveler could spot
Acceptable: To help travelers know the time; to serve as a meeting point; to be a central landmark; to symbolize time
Keeper hint: Think about what a clock does. Why put it where everyone can see it?
Correct: Good reasoning. One token.
At its peak in 1947, how many people used Grand Central Terminal in a single year?
Answer: 65 million
Acceptable: 65 million; 65,000,000
Keeper hint: Michelin NYC Guide - page 180.
Correct: Interesting. That's a token.
The large sculpture above Grand Central's main entrance is called 'The Glory of Commerce.' Which Roman god stands at the center of it?
Answer: Mercury
Acceptable: Mercury; mercury
Keeper hint: Michelin NYC Guide - page 180.
Correct: Exactly. Another token.
Grand Central Terminal has been called the 'Gateway to the ___.' What word completes that phrase?
Answer: Nation
Acceptable: Nation; the nation
Keeper hint: Michelin NYC Guide - page 180.
Correct: Right. One more token.
There's a small dark patch on the ceiling that was left uncleaned on purpose. What does it show?

div.div: Where a skylight was removed decades ago
How dirty the ceiling used to be from train smoke
An old mural that was painted over during renovation
Where a section of plaster collapsed and was patched

div.p: Answer: How dirty the ceiling used to be from train smoke
Acceptable: dirty ceiling; soot from trains; original condition; smoke damage; train smoke; how dirty
Keeper hint: This connects to what you'll need to find later. What was the ceiling like before it was cleaned?
Correct: Good. One token.
Keeper Completion

Alright. You've got the important pieces. Remember what you learned - especially about that ceiling detail. When you arrive at Grand Central, say 'Keeper, we are here' and I'll give you the final challenge. And remember: most people never look up.
Final Challenge / Challenge 3 / On Location
Good. You made it. Look up at the ceiling. Most people never notice what the Griffin spotted years ago.
Clue delivery: Here's what you're looking for.
Somewhere on the main concourse ceiling, there is a small dark patch that was left uncleaned on purpose.
Find it and tell me what it's called.
Hint cost: 2 tokens
Hint: Look up at the ceiling near the northwest corner. It's darker than the rest - left that way on purpose to show what the whole ceiling used to look like before restoration.
What is the dark spot on the ceiling called?
Expected answers: dark patch; the dark patch; dirty patch; soot patch; uncleaned patch
Correct: That's it. Left there on purpose - a reminder of what the whole ceiling looked like before it was cleaned. Good eye, Hunters.
Incorrect: Look up. There's one small spot on the ceiling that's darker than everything around it. What would you call it?
That patch was left on purpose - a quiet reminder of how the station looked before it was restored. The Griffin noticed it years ago. And now you have too.
The Key for this landmark is yours. Claim it and choose your next destination when you're ready.
